observations.statement: Canonical authority follows an explicit owner/consumer rule: owner documents define canon, consumer documents should reference owners rather than reproduce the model, and misleading stale canon should be rewritten outright during packetization and reconciliation.

The PlanUnit contract includes a required `gui_related: true|false` field, owner-adjudication metadata, lossless conversion proof, generated indexes, node-readiness metadata, deterministic finding keys, and repair-closure validation; the subsequent compilation phase is explicitly readiness-only.
Document Sets are contractually composed of a sharded set, `00-index.md`, `manifest.json`, and full audits, with a non-bypassable run failure when verification is breached.

Runtime state authority is divided explicitly: `Run_Modes.md` owns the ask/plan/regular/yolo enum, HTE-versus-DAE selection, budgets, kill conditions, outcomes, and context deltas, while `Goal_Runtime_System.md` owns goal state, scheduling/replanning, visible and invisible execution, child goals, write authority, receipts, certification, verifier/adjudicator policy, and approval-boundary invocation.

The permission contract defines allow/ask/deny actions and an ordered precedence of mode over session over Persona over project over global over defaults, plus last-match-wins granular rules, special guards, persistence, profiles, and Settings > Permissions GUI requirements.

GUI truth is assigned to `FinalGUISpec.md` for layout, responsive behavior, settings placement, chat/activity/plan widgets, browser and terminal surfaces, and Expert/ELI5 behavior; UI wiring separately requires typed UICommands and a one-to-one UI-element-to-UICommandID mapping.

Portable widget composition is constrained to a shared catalog and grid system, while Node Graph is expressly a full-page non-portable Orchestrator tab; only the Orchestrator Progress tab is widget-composed, and a single checklist is identified as the coverage-verification surface for this GUI handoff set.

Persistence and restore authority covers project identity, EventRecord seglog/redb boundaries, workspace tabs and windows, browser/preview state, terminal and dev sessions, plan/TODO/question/activity state, usage projections, and analytics rollups.

Capability ownership is explicit for MVP LSP behavior, requested-versus-effective tool availability, and media operations: LSP is desktop-MVP scope; `Tools.md` owns shared tool semantics; and `Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md` owns capability discovery, uniform generation, route/model capability truth, artifacts, setup hints, and stable errors.

Runtime artifacts and user-project Plan Package outputs are explicitly separate domains: runtime artifacts use runtime events and an artifacts index, whereas Plan Package outputs live under `.puppet-master/project/**` and carry deterministic project-output validation.

Several acceptance-evidence mechanisms are named: the Executor uses a versioned `execution_unit_context` schema and verifier-driven completion; formatter execution emits `format.applied`; shard generation/check and Spec Lock verification have named commands; generated shards/evidence are regeneration-only.

Instant Grep authority is deliberately split among `Tools.md` for query semantics and analytics, `storage-plan.md` for index storage and guards, `FinalGUISpec.md` for indexing/Search UX, and `GitHub_Integration.md` for remote index caching; eight additional documents are designated reconciliation consumers.

The source-control/container packet assigns Git-first Source Control and GitHub Actions to `GitHub_Integration.md`, worktree correctness to `WorktreeGitImprovement.md`, Docker Manager and project-focused Kubernetes placement to `Containers_Registry_and_Unraid.md`, and doctor/result minima to `newtools.md`, with four additional anti-drift companions required.

candidate_findings.summary: The readiness-to-execution gate lacks an exact opening contract.
candidate_findings.obligation: No WorkNodes, executable build tasks, or NodeSeed candidates may be created until the compiler contract is complete and the `PNC-019` executable lifecycle certification harness has passed with recorded evidence.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule does not define what makes the compiler contract complete, the required identity/schema/location of the recorded evidence, or the authority that adjudicates both conditions; those omissions leave consequential discretion over when executable work may begin.

candidate_findings.summary: Post-edit governance validation is conditional on undefined applicability judgments.
candidate_findings.obligation: After canonical edits, generated artifacts must be regenerated or validated as applicable, and packet validation or gates must run as appropriate.
candidate_findings.gap: Although shard and Spec Lock commands are named, the phrases `as applicable` and `as appropriate` do not define trigger conditions, the complete required gate set, pass criteria, or failure handling, allowing builders to omit validation based on their own interpretation.

candidate_findings.summary: The non-bypassable Document Set failure has no exact breach or audit-completeness definition in the capsule.
candidate_findings.obligation: A Document Set must include full audits and must fail the run non-bypassably on a verification breach.
candidate_findings.gap: The index does not identify what constitutes a `full` audit, which verifier produces the breach, the failure state or receipt, or the consumer responsible for enforcing non-bypassability.

candidate_findings.summary: Instant Grep has component owners but no named end-to-end contract or acceptance authority.
candidate_findings.obligation: Query semantics, storage, local GUI behavior, remote caching, and reconciliation consumers must collectively implement one Instant Grep capability.
candidate_findings.gap: The ownership split names four component authorities and eight consumers but does not name an authority for integrated behavior, cross-owner conflict resolution, or end-to-end acceptance evidence, leaving seams such as fallback-to-UI state and remote-cache-to-query behavior to builder discretion.

candidate_findings.summary: The Wiring Matrix authority boundary depends on an undefined content classification.
candidate_findings.obligation: UI elements must follow typed-command rules, while the Wiring Matrix canonically routes producers and consumers and its examples/templates remain subordinate to canonical runtime wiring sections.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule does not identify the referenced runtime wiring sections or specify how to distinguish a canonical routing rule from a subordinate example/template, so conflicting material can be assigned different precedence by different builders.

candidate_findings.summary: Known duplication hotspots have generic guidance but no pair-specific closure contract.
candidate_findings.obligation: Seven named canon/terminology collisions must be reconciled under the owner-doc rule, with stale canon rewritten where references would remain misleading.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule does not map each side of each hotspot to its winning owner, define required migration aliases or replacements, or provide a validation/receipt condition proving that a hotspot is closed.

candidate_findings.summary: Required anti-drift companions for Source Control, GitHub Actions, and Docker Manager lack a satisfaction criterion.
candidate_findings.obligation: Feature-owner documents must be read alongside `newtools.md`, and Contracts, storage, Permissions, and Usage are required anti-drift companions for the packet.
candidate_findings.gap: The packet does not define which companion fields must reconcile, precedence at cross-cutting overlaps, the required validation command, or the receipt that proves all required companions were considered.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: LSP release scope is not ambiguous: it is explicitly MVP and in scope for the desktop release.

Legacy Chain Wizard material is explicitly compatibility/source-lineage only, with current PRD and planning authority assigned to named modern owner documents; `newfeatures.md` is likewise historical/origin material rather than the normative owner for promoted features.
The present Plan-to-Node boundary is explicit about prohibited outputs: it does not create WorkNodes, executable build tasks, or NodeSeed candidates before the stated gate.
Runtime artifacts and Project Plan Package artifacts are explicitly distinguished by authority, storage domain, and purpose.
The portable-widget versus full-page Node Graph distinction and the fact that Progress is the Orchestrator's only widget-composed tab are explicit.
Media capability proof has an explicit negative rule: Cursor image-input proof and media aliases are not provider-availability proof without route, catalog, and artifact evidence.
Generated shard/evidence files have an explicit no-hand-edit rule, and the shard generator/checker and Spec Lock verifier commands are named.
At the feature-owner level, Source Control, GitHub Actions, worktree correctness, Docker Manager, and doctor/result-minimum scopes are assigned to named documents rather than left wholly unowned.

unknowns.statement: Whether the `PNC-019` harness has passed and whether qualifying recorded evidence currently exists cannot be determined from this capsule.
unknowns.reason: The index states the gate but supplies neither current gate state nor an evidence reference.

unknowns.statement: The exact runtime event payloads, attempt states, safe-point fields, remediation-lineage fields, and restart transitions cannot be extracted from this capsule.
unknowns.reason: The index routes those details to Contracts, Executor, storage, GUI, chat/interview, and Glossary owners without reproducing their exact contracts here.

unknowns.statement: The current closure status of the seven listed cross-cutting duplication hotspots is unknown.
unknowns.reason: They are identified as highest-risk hotspots, but no per-hotspot status, closure key, validator result, or receipt is included.

unknowns.reason: The index identifies the checklist as the single confirming table but does not include its rows, evidence, or refresh rule.
